def is_prime(n):
    """Checks if a number n is prime."""
    if n <= 1:
        return False
    if n <= 3:
        return True
    if n % 2 == 0 or n % 3 == 0:
        return False
    i = 5
    while i * i <= n:
        if n % i == 0 or n % (i + 2) == 0:
            return False
        i += 6
    return True

def check_triple(p, q, r):
    """
    Tests if the triple (p, q, r) satisfies the prime conditions.
    Assumes p, q, r are distinct and p < q < r.
    """
    # 1. Check distinctness and ordering (already assumed by caller, but good practice)
    if not (p < q < r and p != q and q != r and p != r):
        return False, "Order or distinctness violation"

    # 2. Check that p, q, r are primes (already assumed by caller, but good practice)
    if not (is_prime(p) and is_prime(q) and is_prime(r)):
        return False, "p, q, or r is not prime"

    # 3. Check the four required values are prime
    P1 = p + q - r
    P2 = q + r - p
    P3 = r + p - q
    P4 = p + q + r

    conditions = {
        "P1 (p+q-r)": P1,
        "P2 (q+r-p)": P2,
        "P3 (r+p-q)": P3,
        "P4 (p+q+r)": P4
    }

    all_primes = True
    failures = {}
    for name, val in conditions.items():
        if not is_prime(val):
            all_primes = False
            failures[name] = val

    if all_primes:
